newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian PZ concludes merger with unit.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian PZ concludes merger with unit.

text.p: Nigerian conglomerate PZ Industries boosted its share capital on Wednesday after concluding its merger with Thermocool Engineering company, one of its subsidiaries.
Some 187,988,262 shares of Thermocool were listed on the Nigerian stock market on Wednesday, further consolidating PZ's position as Nigeria's most capitalised firm.
As at January 17, 1997, it had some 893.5 million shares worth 31.9 billion naira, according to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
PZ shares fell one kobo to 28.55 naira on Wednesday.
The overall market capitalisation as at Tuesday was 292.8 billion naira, said the stock exchange.
Traders said PZ's market capitalisation should now be higher considering the latest addition and a one-for-four bonus issue it declared earlier this month.
They said the merger was aimed at streamlining the management of both concerns, thereby cutting costs, a trend which has become fashionable among quoted Nigerian companies.
PZ manufactures and markets a wide range of consumer items while Thermocool produces refrigerating equipment as well as packaging materials for PZ products.
Officials of the company were not immediately available for comments.
Traders said foreign shareholders seemed to be consolidating their positions in their Nigerian interests following new laws that allow for foreign ownership of businesses.
"Foreign owners are trying to beef up their stake in companies having prospects," one said.
Beginning last year, some leading firms have concluded mergers with local subsidiaries or with independent concerns.

These include Lever Brothers which swallowed A.J. Seward, a division of Unilever Nigeria Ltd., Nestle Foods took over Nestle Nigeria Ltd., Smithkline Beecham which bought Sterling Products and Nigerian Bottling Company which merged with Sapanda Nigeria Ltd.
